program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate and run heavy validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and abstract verification
PMID-level dedupe against cumulative Wave 2000 index and rolling deep-state

waves.focus: Systematic review of Australian residential aged-care medication use found no published studies reporting melatonin prevalence and only limited unpublished estimates, while benzodiazepine/Z-drug use was common; this is utilization evidence, not melatonin efficacy.

Meta-analysis of clinical trials in adults over 60 found inhaled lavender improved subjective sleep-quality scores, but heterogeneity was very high and all included studies used inhalation, limiting generalization to oral lavender products.

Meta-analysis of 9 RCTs found Ginkgo biloba extract modestly reduced dizziness/vertigo severity and improved some functional outcomes in central neurologic disorders, but populations were heterogeneous and predominantly dementia-related.

Female-specific multilevel meta-analysis found small positive average effects of creatine on selected performance and body-composition outcomes, with uncertain physiological effects; heterogeneity and low or very-low certainty prevent firm sport-specific conclusions.

Systematic review mapped SLC22A5 variant pathogenicity in primary carnitine deficiency and linked severe truncating variants with early cardiomyopathy; this is genetic disease-context evidence rather than evidence for routine L-carnitine supplementation.

Meta-analysis of seven clinical trials found magnesium supplementation modestly reduced ALT and AST but not GGT or alkaline phosphatase; heterogeneity was extremely high for ALT and AST, limiting clinical interpretation.

Review described extensive preclinical mechanisms and chemosensitizing potential for berberine in breast cancer but emphasized pharmacokinetic limitations and translational barriers; it does not establish human anticancer efficacy.

Meta-analysis of 18 RCTs involving 10,195 infants found probiotic supplementation initiated only during infancy did not significantly prevent atopic dermatitis; prior positive prevention signals appear driven largely by maternal-plus-infant regimens.

Meta-analysis of adult asthma RCTs found probiotics/prebiotics/synbiotics modestly improved FEV1 measures but not asthma-control scores, with inconsistent inflammatory markers and low-to-moderate certainty; evidence does not justify routine use.

Systematic review of case reports linked psychosis-related restrictive intake and self-neglect with vitamin C deficiency/scurvy; vitamin C repletion improved physical scurvy manifestations, but case evidence cannot quantify psychiatric treatment effects.

Meta-analysis of case-control studies found no significant association between maternal iron supplementation during pregnancy and childhood acute leukemia, including AML and ALL; this is observational safety evidence.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of recreational nitrous-oxide cases found functional vitamin B12 deficiency commonly presented with neurologic abnormalities even when serum B12 or hematologic indices were normal; methylmalonic acid and homocysteine were more sensitive markers.

Meta-analysis of 27 RCTs found curcumin/turmeric produced modest improvements in triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, and HDL-C in prediabetes/diabetes, but heterogeneity exceeded 80% and certainty was low for all outcomes.

Meta-analysis of 34 RCTs reported symptom and recurrence improvements with the multi-herb Si Shen Wan formula alone or with other therapies for IBS-D, but trial quality, blinding, follow-up, and complex formulation limit ingredient-level conclusions.

Meta-analysis found neonatal phototherapy was associated with lower serum calcium and magnesium and substantial rates of hypocalcemia/hypomagnesemia, while vitamin D changes were inconclusive; evidence certainty was low and routine supplementation was not supported.

Meta-analysis of 14 RCTs in people with mental disorders found Ashwagandha improved anxiety and showed signals for depression, stress, and sleep, but small studies, heterogeneity, and outlier effects limited certainty; Bayesian confirmation was strongest for anxiety.

Meta-analysis of 18 RCTs found adjunctive melatonin with nonsurgical periodontal therapy improved some attachment and pocket-depth outcomes at selected time points, but prediction intervals crossed the null and heterogeneity limited confidence in consistent benefit.

Meta-analysis of 63 studies found creatine plus resistance training improved upper- and lower-body strength and lean mass versus training alone, with no significant fat-mass effect; exploratory age moderation and heterogeneous nutrition/training backgrounds limit individualized prescriptions.

Systematic review found no eligible protein-supplementation studies in children with cancer and only very low-certainty evidence from other chronically or critically ill pediatric populations, documenting a major evidence gap rather than efficacy.
Meta-analysis of 9 RCTs found omega-3 added to scaling/root planing modestly improved periodontal pocket depth and attachment level, but heterogeneity was substantial and overall certainty was low.

Scoping review found heterogeneous evidence suggesting myo-inositol may improve some PCOS metabolic and fertility-related outcomes, while oocyte/embryo-quality results remained inconsistent; no formal risk-of-bias appraisal or quantitative synthesis was performed.

Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs in colorectal-cancer surgery found probiotics reduced several infectious/GI complications and improved intestinal-barrier markers, but some outcomes were null and sensitivity analyses showed variability; evidence is perioperative oncology-specific.

Meta-analysis of 155 RCTs found probiotics produced modest average reductions in triglycerides, total cholesterol, and LDL-C and a small HDL-C increase; the class-wide pooling spans many strains and formulations, so effects should not be treated as interchangeable across products.

Updated Cochrane review found antenatal magnesium sulfate for women at risk of preterm birth reduced cerebral palsy and death-or-cerebral-palsy through two years, while maternal treatment-stopping adverse effects increased; evidence concerns clinical perinatal magnesium therapy, not routine oral supplementation.

Meta-analysis of 13 RCTs found pooled antioxidant supplements improved several insulin-resistance indices in gestational diabetes, but interventions spanned selenium, alpha-lipoic acid, zinc, and EGCG with substantial heterogeneity, preventing ingredient-level attribution.
